nodes.name: Pixel
documentation: Pixel stores one eight bit red, green, blue, and alpha sample. Fully
transparent black is its ordinary default.

nodes.name: Point2D
documentation: Point2D remains distinct from a general Math vector even though both carry
two real values.

nodes.name: Size2D
documentation: Zero width or height carries the ordinary unconfigured state rather than a
target allocation.

nodes.name: Tone
documentation: Opaque white preserves the source color unchanged.

nodes.name: Transform2D
documentation: Transform2D carries translation, scale, and rotation without choosing a
backend matrix representation.

nodes.name: Placement2D
documentation: Placement2D lets Graphics read the transform and frame ordering of a real
Object without implying that the Object hosts children or contributes a draw.

nodes.name: Image
documentation: Image is a decoded RGBA value whose immutable pixel Object is shared by value copies.
Its size and addressing policy give those pixels graphics meaning while Vulkan remains
responsible for device images and uploads.

nodes.name: Texture2D
documentation: Texture2D gives one Image a durable rendering identity. Graphics backends
realize device storage from this Object while the image and sampling meaning
remain independent from any Vulkan handle.

nodes.name: Sprite
documentation: Sprite keeps its concrete Shader Instance through the TexturedQuad2D Render
contract. An empty Shader or texture contributes no draw without changing
the Sprite identity.

nodes.name: PNG
documentation: PNG names the encoded format at the native boundary. Image remains the
decoded graphics value, so another codec can produce the same Type without
adding format behavior to Image itself.

nodes.name: Vec2D
documentation: Vec2D stores two ordered R32 components named x and y.
It remains a general vector so domain Packages can build points, sizes, and
other meanings without changing this shared Type.

nodes.name: Vec3D
documentation: Vec3D stores three ordered R32 components named x, y, and z.
It remains a general vector so domain Packages can add their own spatial or
color meaning without changing this shared Type.

nodes.name: Vec4D
documentation: Vec4D stores four ordered R32 components named x, y, z, and w.
Its neutral shape lets CPU and GPU contracts share one Type while each
domain retains the meaning it assigns to those components.

nodes.name: Bytes
documentation: Bytes is a copy on write container of U8 values local to one worker.
It retains one Object buffer and a separate logical size. Self operations
mutate the receiver by reference and return that same reference for chaining.
Read only Views do not extend the Object lifetime and cannot be retained
across an operation that can replace the backing Object.

documentation: Dynamic values backed by the Perimortem Memory ABI.

nodes.name: <source>
documentation: Dynamic values backed by the Perimortem Memory ABI.

nodes.name: Bytes
documentation: Bytes is a copy on write container of U8 values local to one worker.
It retains one Object buffer and a separate logical size. Self operations
mutate the receiver by reference and return that same reference for chaining.
Read only Views do not extend the Object lifetime and cannot be retained
across an operation that can replace the backing Object.

nodes.name: concat
documentation: Creates an independent Bytes containing every element of left followed by
every element of right. Neither input View is modified.

nodes.name: copy
documentation: Creates an independent Bytes containing every element of view.

nodes.name: with_capacity
documentation: Creates an empty Bytes whose backing Object can hold at least the requested
number of elements without another allocation.

nodes.name: append
nodes.declaration: func append[.self : Bytes, .byte : U8, .count : U64] -> [.self : Bytes]
documentation: Appends count copies of byte and returns this receiver for chaining.
A zero count leaves both the logical size and backing Object unchanged.

nodes.name: clear
documentation: Sets the logical size to zero without overwriting or releasing capacity.

nodes.name: proxy
documentation: Replaces this value with an independent copy of view.

nodes.name: concat
documentation: Appends every element of view and returns this receiver for chaining.
An empty View leaves both the logical size and backing Object unchanged.

nodes.name: detach
documentation: Gives this value a private backing Object while preserving every logical
byte. Native writable views use this operation before exposing an address.

nodes.name: get_capacity
documentation: Returns the number of byte elements available in the backing Object.
Capacity may be greater than the logical size.

nodes.name: get_size
documentation: Returns the number of bytes in the logical value.

nodes.name: get_view
documentation: Borrows a read only View over exactly the logical bytes.

nodes.name: at
documentation: Returns one element when it is available and the U8 default otherwise.

nodes.name: is_empty
documentation: Returns whether the logical size is zero.

nodes.name: reserve
documentation: Ensures capacity is at least required_size without changing logical size.
Existing capacity is left alone when the Object already has enough room.

nodes.name: resize
documentation: Changes the logical size and grows capacity when required.
Existing initialized capacity is preserved. Newly allocated elements use
the U8 default.

nodes.name: forgetful_resize
documentation: Changes the logical size without preserving a backing Object that is shared
or far larger than the requested value.

nodes.name: shrink
documentation: Removes count bytes from the front and shifts the remaining bytes to zero.
Removing at least the logical size is equivalent to clear.

nodes.name: slice
documentation: Borrows the available portion of one logical interval.
The result is clipped at the logical size and is empty when start is out
of bounds.

nodes.name: set
documentation: Fills every logical element with one byte value.

nodes.name: convert
nodes.declaration: func convert[.self : Bytes, .selected : U8, .target : U8] -> [.self : Bytes]
documentation: Replaces each matching logical element without changing the size.

nodes.name: reset
documentation: Releases the backing Object and restores the empty default value.

nodes.name: Key
documentation: Key values keep the same order as the native input boundary. Text entry
remains a separate layout aware concern, while controls can keep stable
identities across platforms.

nodes.name: Input
documentation: Input is copied once from the runtime at a frame boundary. Its state remains
unchanged until the caller asks for the next snapshot, which keeps repeated
queries deterministic throughout Scene update and event delivery.
